newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to deliver food aid to North on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to deliver food aid to North on Thursday.

text.p: South Korea will deliver food aid to the famine-threatened North from Thursday under the first direct agreement between the Red Cross societies of the cold war rivals, local media said on Sunday.
The Hankook Ilbo said the North Korean Red Cross agreed to accept last Monday's offer by its southern counterpart to deliver 11,200 tonnes of food from June 12 to 19 via China.
Officials at the South Korean Red Cross were not available for comment.
The Red Cross societies of the two Koreas signed an agreement last month in Beijing to ship 50,000 tonnes of food aid, mostly corn, to the North by the end of July.
Under the accord, the aid would be transported through two ports in North Korea and also by land across the isolated nation's border with China.
The daily said the North Korean Red Cross would send a security guarantee for South Korean Red Cross officials to the truce village of Panmunjom on Monday.
It also said the North Korean consulate in Beijing would issue a visa for South Korean officials.

Capitalist Seoul and communist Pyongyang have been technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean civil war ended only in a truce. Decades of mutual mistrust have made even basic food aid a delicate diplomatic affair.
U.N. agencies say North Korea faces a food crisis after two years of flooding wiped out crops and that isolated deaths from malnutrition are already being reported.
